about.ex: The bus ride takes about twenty minutes.

accommodation.en: a place to live or stay
accommodation.ex: The college offers accommodation to first-year students.

account.en: form a part of a total; be included in a count
account.ex: Students account for half the users.
account.zh: 佔（account for：佔…比例）；（accounted for：被計入）

accounted.en: included in a count (be accounted for)

acknowledged.ex: He acknowledged that the plan had problems.

across.es: en todo; a lo largo de

action.en: things done; industrial action: strikes or protest by workers
action.zh: 行動（industrial action：勞資爭議行動）

acute.ex: There is an acute shortage of nurses.

example.en: There is an acute shortage of nurses in rural areas.
example.zh: 鄉村地區護理人員嚴重短缺。

note.usage: 常修飾 shortage, problem, pressure；醫學上指「急性的」。

noteEs.exampleTr: Hay una grave escasez de enfermeras en zonas rurales.
noteEs.usage: acute shortage, acute problem; en medicina 'agudo'.

noteHi.exampleTr: ग्रामीण क्षेत्रों में नर्सों की भारी कमी है।
noteHi.usage: acute shortage/problem आम हैं; चिकित्सा में 'तीव्र'।

noteJa.exampleTr: 地方では看護師が深刻に不足している。
noteJa.usage: acute shortage/problem の形。医学では「急性」。

adhering.ex: Players must adhere to the rules of the game.

example.en: All staff must adhere to the safety guidelines.
example.zh: 所有員工都必須遵守安全指引。

note.meaning: 嚴格遵守規則、協議或計畫。
note.usage: 固定搭配 adhere to + 規則；名詞為 adherence。比 follow 正式。

noteEn.meaning: to follow a rule or plan exactly.
noteEn.usage: Always 'adhere to' something; more formal than 'follow'.

noteEs.exampleTr: Todo el personal debe cumplir las normas de seguridad.
noteEs.usage: Siempre con to: adhere to the rules. Más formal que follow.

noteHi.exampleTr: सभी कर्मचारियों को सुरक्षा दिशानिर्देशों का पालन करना होगा।
noteHi.meaning: नियमों का सख़्ती से पालन करना।
noteHi.usage: हमेशा adhere to + नियम के साथ प्रयोग होता है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 全職員は安全指針を守らなければならない。
noteJa.meaning: 規則や合意を厳守する。
noteJa.usage: adhere to + 規則 の形。follow より硬い表現。

noteKo.exampleTr: 모든 직원은 안전 지침을 준수해야 한다.
noteKo.usage: adhere to + 규칙 형태. follow보다 격식체.

admitted.ex: The company admitted that prices were too high.

adults.ex: Tickets cost ten dollars for adults.

affecting.en: having an influence or effect on
affecting.ex: The new rule is affecting many small shops.

also.ex: She speaks French and also Spanish.

appear.ex: Stars appear when the sky gets dark.

approximately.en: close to a number, not exact
approximately.ex: The trip takes approximately three hours.

argued.ex: He argued that taxes were too high.

around.ex: Around fifty people came to the party.

as.en: in the same way; in the role of

asked.ex: The teacher asked us about our weekend.

assistance.en: help, often money from the State
assistance.ex: The State offers assistance with rent.

at.en: in a place, time or level

attributing.ex: She attributes her success to hard work.

example.en: The company attributed the losses to high energy costs.
example.zh: 該公司將虧損歸因於高昂的能源成本。

note.usage: 常用 attribute A to B（把A歸因於B）；新聞中常見 attribute the delay/rise to...。

noteEn.meaning: to say that something is caused by something else.

noteEs.exampleTr: La empresa atribuyó las pérdidas a los altos costes de energía.
noteEs.usage: Estructura: attribute A to B (atribuir A a B).

noteHi.exampleTr: कंपनी ने घाटे का कारण ऊँची ऊर्जा लागत बताया।
noteHi.meaning: किसी बात का कारण किसी चीज़ को बताना।
noteHi.usage: attribute A to B: A का कारण B बताना।

noteJa.exampleTr: 会社は損失を高いエネルギー費のせいだとした。
noteJa.meaning: ある事柄の原因を〜だとする。
noteJa.usage: attribute A to B（AをBのせいにする）の形が基本。

noteKo.exampleTr: 회사는 손실을 높은 에너지 비용 탓으로 돌렸다.
noteKo.usage: attribute A to B(A를 B 탓으로 돌리다) 형태로 쓴다.

august.en: the eighth month of the year

authorities.ex: The authorities closed the road after the storm.

avoid.ex: Try to avoid driving during rush hour.

barriers.en: things that make it hard to do something
barriers.ex: High costs are barriers for small firms.

be.ex: Try to be on time tomorrow.

been.ex: It has been a busy week.

blaming.ex: Don't blame the weather for being late.

called.en: asked someone to do something (call on)
called.ex: They called on the minister to act.

capital.en: the main city of a country
capital.ex: Dublin is the capital of Ireland.

cent.ex: Prices rose by five per cent.

challenges.ex: Big cities face many housing challenges.

check.en: look at something to make sure it is right
check.ex: Please check your answers before you finish.

citizens.en: people who belong to a country
citizens.ex: Senior citizens get free bus rides.

clarify.en: make something clear and easy to understand
clarify.ex: Could you clarify what you mean?

clearly.en: in a way that is easy to understand

collect.ex: The council collects data every month.

collectively.ex: The three shops collectively employ 50 people.

come.en: come onto the market: go on sale
come.ex: New phones come onto the market every year.

commit.ex: The city did not commit to a date.

compiled.en: collected and put together from different information
compiled.ex: The list was compiled from police records.

complete.ex: We need a complete list of names.

example.en: The report gives a comprehensive picture of the problem.
example.zh: 這份報告完整呈現了問題全貌。

note.usage: 常修飾 data, review, plan, report；比 complete 更正式。

noteEs.exampleTr: El informe ofrece una visión completa del problema.
noteEs.usage: Suele acompañar a data, review, plan.

noteHi.exampleTr: रिपोर्ट समस्या की व्यापक तस्वीर देती है।
noteHi.usage: data, review, plan जैसे शब्दों के साथ आम।

noteJa.exampleTr: 報告書は問題の全体像を示している。
noteJa.usage: data, review, plan などと結びつく。

noteKo.exampleTr: 보고서는 문제의 전체 그림을 보여 준다.
noteKo.usage: data, review, plan 등과 함께 쓴다.

comprising.ex: Women are comprising half of the group.

conceded.en: admitted that something is true, often unwillingly
conceded.ex: He conceded that the test was too hard.

consequently.ex: It rained all day; consequently, the match was cancelled.

contingent.ex: The deal is contingent upon approval.

example.en: Our plans are contingent upon the weather.
example.zh: 我們的計畫取決於天氣。

note.meaning: 取決於某條件的；視…而定。
note.usage: 常用 be contingent upon/on + 名詞；學術寫作中常用來表達條件關係。

noteEs.usage: Se usa be contingent upon/on + sustantivo; típico del registro académico.

noteHi.exampleTr: हमारी योजनाएँ मौसम पर निर्भर हैं।
noteHi.usage: be contingent upon/on + संज्ञा के रूप में प्रयोग।

noteJa.exampleTr: 私たちの計画は天気次第だ。
noteJa.usage: be contingent upon/on + 名詞。学術的な文章で多用。

noteKo.usage: be contingent upon/on + 명사. 학술적 글에서 자주 쓴다.

councils.en: local governments for a town or area

count.ex: Please count the people in the room.

counted.ex: The teacher counted the students in the room.

counting.en: adding up; double counting: counting twice
counting.ex: Double counting can make the total too high.

covering.ex: The report, covering ten years, is long.

currently.ex: She is currently living in Cork.

data.en: facts and numbers collected for study
data.ex: The app collects data about your sleep.

date.ex: What is the date of the meeting?

dearth.ex: There is a dearth of cheap homes.

declined.ex: She declined to answer the question.

decrease.ex: There was a decrease in sales.

delay.en: a time when something happens later
delay.ex: There was a short delay before take-off.

democrats.en: members of a democratic party (Social Democrats)

department.ex: The Department of Education sets the rules.

did.en: past of 'do'; also helps form questions and negatives
did.ex: Voters did not register by party.

do.ex: Workers do less when they are unhappy.

does.ex: He does his homework after dinner.
does.zh: 做；進行（does a survey：做調查）

double.en: having two parts at the same time
double.ex: The town faces a double problem of floods and fires.

drift.en: move slowly without a clear plan
drift.ex: Some young people drift between jobs.

due.ex: The report is due next week.

duplication.en: counting or doing the same thing twice
duplication.ex: We must avoid duplication of work.

earliest.zh: 最早的（at the earliest opportunity：盡早）

emergency.en: for dangerous situations needing quick action

emphasised.en: said something strongly to show importance
emphasised.ex: She emphasised the need for safety.

ensure.ex: Please ensure the door is locked.

entitled.ex: You are entitled to a refund.

example.en: Every worker is entitled to paid holidays.
example.zh: 每位勞工都有權享有帶薪假。

note.usage: be entitled to + 名詞 / to do；名詞 entitlement。

noteEn.meaning: having the right to have or do something.

noteEs.exampleTr: Todo trabajador tiene derecho a vacaciones pagadas.
noteEs.usage: be entitled to + sustantivo o infinitivo.

noteHi.exampleTr: हर कर्मचारी सवेतन छुट्टी का हक़दार है।

noteJa.exampleTr: すべての労働者は有給休暇を取る権利がある。
noteJa.meaning: 権利がある；資格がある。
noteJa.usage: be entitled to + 名詞/to do。

noteKo.exampleTr: 모든 근로자는 유급 휴가를 받을 권리가 있다.
noteKo.usage: be entitled to + 명사/to do 형태.

explained.ex: The teacher explained the rules clearly.

failed.ex: The talks failed to produce a deal.

fall.ex: There was a fall in house prices.

figure.ex: The figure for Dublin is higher.

figures.ex: The new figures will come out next week.

find.ex: It is hard to find a cheap flat.

frequently.ex: Buses run frequently in the city.

frustrated.en: annoyed because you cannot do what you want
frustrated.ex: Drivers grew frustrated by the long traffic jam.

frustration.en: feeling annoyed because you cannot do something

fully.ex: The hotel is fully booked this weekend.

furthermore.ex: The flat is cheap; furthermore, it is near work.

give.ex: The new law gives tenants more rights.

given.ex: The school has given a warning about ice.

government.en: the group of people who run a country
government.ex: The government will build new schools.

greater.ex: Teachers want greater support from parents.

gripping.en: strongly affecting a place or group
gripping.ex: A cold spell is gripping the country.
gripping.ja: 覆っている；苦しめている

guard.en: try to stop something bad (guard against)
guard.ex: Wash your hands to guard against illness.

had.en: possessed; was involved (had a hand in)
had.ex: She had a key role in the project.

hard.ex: It was hard to hear in the noise.

harder.ex: The rain made the walk harder.

has.en: owns or holds; also forms perfect tense

have.ja: 持つ；〜しなければならない

held.ex: The train was held up by snow.

high.ex: Prices are high in tourist areas.

hold-up.ex: Sorry for the hold-up at the start.

home.en: the place where you live (Home Furnishings)
home.ex: They sell goods for the home.

homeless.en: having no home to live in

homelessness.en: the problem of having no home
homelessness.ex: Homelessness has risen in many cities.

homes.ex: New homes are being built near the river.

housed.ex: The families were housed in a hotel.

housing.en: homes for people to live in
housing.ex: The city needs more cheap housing.

how.ex: Show me how this machine works.

however.ex: It was sunny; however, it was cold.

impediment.ex: Cost is the main impediment to change.

example.en: High costs are a major impediment to growth.
example.zh: 高成本是成長的一大阻礙。

note.usage: an impediment to + 名詞；比 obstacle 更正式。

noteEs.exampleTr: Los altos costes son un gran impedimento para el crecimiento.
noteEs.usage: an impediment to...; más formal que obstacle.

noteHi.exampleTr: ऊँची लागत विकास में बड़ी बाधा है।
noteHi.usage: an impediment to + संज्ञा; obstacle से औपचारिक।

noteJa.exampleTr: 高コストは成長の大きな障害だ。
noteJa.usage: an impediment to 〜。obstacle より硬い。

noteKo.usage: an impediment to ~ 형태. obstacle보다 격식체.

increase.ex: There was a 10% increase in sales.

increased.ex: Increased traffic has made the roads busy.

indefinitely.en: for a time with no fixed end

industrial.zh: 勞資的（industrial action：勞資爭議行動）

insisting.en: saying firmly that something is true
insisting.ex: He kept insisting he was right.

interview.en: a meeting where someone answers questions
interview.ex: She gave an interview to the local paper.

interviewed.ex: He was interviewed on television last night.

jobs.ex: The new factory will create 500 jobs.

larger.ex: They moved to a larger house.

last.ex: We went to Spain last summer.

latest.ex: Have you read her latest book?

lead.ex: She is the lead author of the report.

living.en: having your home in a place

lot.ex: She drinks a lot of water every day.

maintained.en: said firmly that something is true
maintained.ex: He maintained that the plan was fair.

make.en: to produce; make use of: use
make.ex: Factories make cheap versions of popular drugs.
make.ja: 作る；（make use of）利用する

makes.ex: The company makes software for schools.

many.ex: Many people work from home now.

means.ex: Staff means everyone who works here.

minister.en: a leader of a government department
minister.ex: The minister visited the new school.

missed.ex: Nobody should be missed from the list.

month.ex: The rent is due each month.

monthly.ex: She pays a monthly fee for the gym.

most.en: used to make the superlative: to the greatest degree
most.ex: This is the most beautiful beach in Spain.

move.en: go or take to another place
move.ex: They want to move families into homes.
move.zh: 搬移；（move in and out：進出）

moving.ex: The traffic is moving slowly this morning.

must.ex: You must wear a seatbelt in the car.

nationally.ex: The show is broadcast nationally every Friday.

net.en: a system meant to catch everyone (slip through the net)
net.ex: The new rules close gaps in the safety net.
net.zh: 網（slip through the net：被漏掉）

nevertheless.ex: It was raining; nevertheless, we went out.

non-irish.ex: Many non-Irish workers live in Dublin.
non-irish.ja: アイルランド国籍以外の

not.ex: I do not like cold tea.

noted.ex: She noted that prices were falling.
noted.zh: 注意到；指出（it should be noted：值得注意的是）

number.ex: The number of tourists is rising.

obstacle.ex: Language can be an obstacle for new arrivals.

obstacles.ex: Cost and time are big obstacles.

obtain.ex: You must obtain a permit first.

obtaining.ex: Obtaining a visa can take months.

official.en: approved by the government or an authority
official.ex: The official report came out today.

officials.ex: Officials met to discuss the plan.

on.ex: Voting will go on for nine days.

operating.en: carrying out a system or rule
operating.ex: The union is operating an overtime ban.

opportunity.en: a chance to do something good
opportunity.ex: This job is a great opportunity for her.

out.en: made public (come out); away from a place
out.ex: The new figures will come out on Friday.

paid.ex: Nurses are paid every two weeks.

part.ex: Cost is only part of the reason.

particularly.ex: It was particularly cold last night.

parts.ex: The main parts of the house are built.

pay.ex: It is hard to pay for a home in Dublin.

payment.ex: The payment is due in May.

per.ex: The ticket costs ten euro per person.

planned.ex: The planned trip was cancelled because of rain.

pledging.ex: The mayor is pledging more money for parks.

point.en: show a direction; point to: name as a cause
point.ex: The data point to a slow recovery.
point.zh: 指向（point upwards：顯示上升）；指出

pointed.en: named something as a cause (pointed to)
pointed.ex: She pointed to rising costs as the problem.

postponed.ex: The match was postponed because of snow.

predict.en: say what will happen in the future
predict.ex: Nobody can predict the weather perfectly.

pressed.ex: Reporters pressed her for an answer.

prevent.ex: Rules prevent managers from hiring staff.

previously.ex: She previously worked in a bank.

principal.ex: The principal aim is to cut costs.

private.en: not owned or run by the government
private.ex: She works for a private company.

properties.en: buildings and land owned by someone
properties.ex: Property prices are rising fast in the suburbs.

proportion.ex: A large proportion of staff work from home.

example.en: A large proportion of students work part-time.
example.zh: 很大比例的學生兼職工作。

note.usage: the proportion of A（A的比例）；a large/small proportion；比 share 更正式，學術寫作常用。

noteEn.meaning: a part of a total, often as a percentage.

noteEs.exampleTr: Una gran proporción de estudiantes trabaja a tiempo parcial.
noteEs.usage: the proportion of...; a large proportion. Más formal que share.

noteHi.exampleTr: छात्रों का बड़ा हिस्सा अंशकालिक काम करता है।
noteHi.usage: the proportion of + संज्ञा; a large proportion।

noteJa.exampleTr: 学生の大部分がアルバイトをしている。
noteJa.usage: the proportion of 〜；a large proportion の形。

noteKo.usage: the proportion of ~; a large proportion 형태. share보다 격식체.

public.ex: The library is a public building.

publication.en: making something available to the public
publication.ex: The publication of the report was delayed.

publish.en: to make information available to the public
publish.ex: Schools must publish their exam results.

published.ex: The report was published on Monday.

put.ex: Put your name on the form.
put.zh: 放；（put on the website：放上網站）

radio.en: programmes you listen to, not watch
radio.ex: I listen to the radio every morning.

ready.en: finished and able to be used

recent.ex: In recent years, prices have risen.

record.en: the highest ever level (a record high)
record.ex: Prices hit a record high in May.
record.zh: 紀錄（a record high：歷史新高）

recorded.ex: The hottest day was recorded in July.

relating.ex: The data relating to August is final.

release.ex: The release of the report was delayed.

relocating.en: moving something to a new place
relocating.ex: The company is relocating its office to the city centre.

rent.en: to pay money to live in a place
rent.ex: Many students rent a room near college.

rental.ex: Rental homes are hard to find in Dublin.

report.ex: Councils report the numbers each month.

reported.ex: The minister reported a big rise.

residing.ex: People residing abroad can vote by post.

returns.ex: Councils send their returns every month.

revealed.ex: The report revealed a big drop in sales.

right.en: something you are allowed to do
right.ex: Everyone has the right to vote.

rigorous.ex: New drugs go through rigorous testing.

example.en: All new medicines go through rigorous testing.
example.zh: 所有新藥都經過嚴格測試。

note.usage: 常見 rigorous checks/testing/analysis；用來強調方法仔細可靠。

noteEs.exampleTr: Todos los medicamentos nuevos pasan pruebas rigurosas.

noteHi.exampleTr: सभी नई दवाओं की कठोर जाँच होती है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 新薬はすべて厳格な試験を受ける。

rise.ex: There was a rise in prices.

rté.en: Ireland's national TV and radio company
rté.ja: RTÉ（アイルランド国営放送）
rté.zh: RTÉ 愛爾蘭國家廣播電視台

s.en: shows that something belongs to someone

said.ex: She said the shop was closed.

say.ex: He could not say when it would end.

saying.ex: He left, saying he was tired.

scarcity.ex: The scarcity of water hurt the farms.

example.en: The scarcity of affordable homes pushes up rents.
example.zh: 平價住宅的短缺推高了租金。

note.usage: 形容詞 scarce；常見 scarcity of + 名詞，學術寫作中常用以替代 shortage。

noteEn.meaning: a situation where there is not enough of something.

noteEs.exampleTr: La escasez de viviendas asequibles hace subir los alquileres.

noteHi.exampleTr: सस्ते घरों की कमी किराया बढ़ाती है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 手頃な住宅の不足が家賃を押し上げる。

schedule.en: a plan of when things will happen

scheduled.ex: The meeting is scheduled for Monday.

scheme.en: an official plan from the government

sector.ex: She works in the health sector.

secure.ex: She secured a place at college.

securing.ex: She secured a place at university.

service.en: the people who work for the State (public service)
service.ex: She works in the public service.

set.en: a group of things that belong together
set.ex: We need a full set of results.

share.ex: Women make up a larger share of students.

shares.ex: The office shares the results online.

shortage.en: a situation where there is not enough
shortage.ex: There is a shortage of teachers in rural areas.

showed.ex: She showed her plan to the team.

significant.en: large or important enough to notice
significant.ex: There was a significant rise in prices.

significantly.ex: Prices have risen significantly this year.

singled.en: chose one thing for special attention (single out)
singled.ex: The report singled out poor planning.

slips.en: is missed by a system (slip through the net)
slips.ex: No child should slip through the net.

so.ex: It was raining, so we stayed home.

social.en: about society and people living together
social.ex: Poverty is a big social problem.

socio-economic.en: about money and social position together

some.en: a number of, but not all

speaking.ex: Speaking up early can stop a conflict.

specify.ex: Please specify the date of your arrival.

spoke.ex: The minister spoke about the plan.

staff.en: the people who work for an organisation
staff.ex: The staff are on strike today.

stands.en: is at a certain level (stands at)

state.ex: The State pays for public schools.

state-funded.ex: She studied at a state-funded school.

statistics.en: numbers that give facts about something
statistics.ex: Statistics show more people cycle to work.

stay.ex: Most tourists stay in the centre.

steeper.ex: They face steeper costs than others.

stressed.en: said strongly that it is important
stressed.ex: She stressed the need for care.

submitted.ex: She submitted her report on time.

substantial.ex: The new road needs a substantial amount of money.

example.en: There has been a substantial increase in rents.

note.usage: 常修飾 increase, amount, number；學術寫作中比 big 更正式。

noteEs.exampleTr: Ha habido un aumento considerable de los alquileres.

noteHi.exampleTr: किराए में काफ़ी वृद्धि हुई है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 家賃が大幅に上がった。
noteJa.usage: increase, amount, number などと結びつく。

noteKo.usage: increase, amount, number 등과 함께 쓴다.

sunday.ex: We visit my grandparents on Sunday.

sure.en: make sure: check that it happens
sure.ex: Are you sure about the time?

taking.ex: She is taking her driving test.

tallies.ex: The office tallies the votes each night.

tasks.ex: I have three tasks to finish today.

tend.ex: Prices tend to rise in winter.

there.ex: We went to the park and played there.

these.en: the ones here or just mentioned

through.ex: They bought it through a special deal.

too.ex: The coffee is too hot to drink.

total.ex: The total cost was two million.

paragraphs: Every month, the Government shares the number of homeless people in Ireland. This month, the numbers did not come out.
Some public workers are taking part in a work-to-rule. They only do the main parts of their jobs. Because of this, some councils did not send their numbers.
James Browne is the Minister for Housing. He said he was frustrated. He does not know when the numbers will come out.
In August, a record 17,885 people were in emergency housing. This included 5,830 children.
Mr Browne also said that about half of these people are not Irish citizens. In Dublin, it is 58%. He said they have every right to a home. But it is hard to find homes to rent, especially in Dublin.
sentZh: 政府每個月都會公布愛爾蘭無家可歸者的人數。
這個月，數字沒有公布。
部分公務人員正在進行依法怠工。
他們只做工作中最主要的部分。
因此，有些地方議會沒有送出數字。
詹姆斯．布朗是住房部長。
他說他感到很沮喪。
他不知道數字何時會公布。
八月時，有創紀錄的17,885人住在緊急安置住所。
其中包括5,830名兒童。
布朗也說，這些人當中約有一半不是愛爾蘭公民。
在都柏林，比例是58%。
他說他們完全有權利擁有住所。
但要找到可租的房子很難，尤其是在都柏林。

paragraphs: The Government did not publish its monthly homeless figures on Friday as planned. The Department of Housing said this was because of industrial action by some public sector workers.

The workers are on a work-to-rule, which means they only do the tasks that are strictly part of their jobs. The department said it had not received numbers from all nine regional councils that collect the data. These councils count the people who stay in emergency accommodation paid for by the State.

James Browne, the Minister for Housing, spoke about the delay on RTÉ radio on Sunday. He said he was frustrated that the figures could not be released. He explained that people can move in and out of homelessness, so the department must check carefully that nobody is counted twice or missed. He could not say when the numbers will be ready, but he promised to publish them as soon as possible.
The last official figures, for August, showed a record 17,885 people in emergency accommodation. Of these, 12,055 were adults and 5,830 were children.

Mr Browne also said that the share of non-Irish citizens in emergency accommodation has risen a lot. Around half of the people in this accommodation across the country are not Irish citizens, and in Dublin the figure is 58%. He said these people have every right to housing, but they often find it harder to pay for a home.

The minister said there are too few homes to rent, especially in Dublin, and this makes it difficult to move families out of emergency accommodation. The Social Democrats had asked him to say clearly when the September figures would come out.
sentZh: 政府週五沒有如期公布每月的無家可歸者數據。
住房部表示，這是因為部分公部門員工採取了勞資爭議行動。
這些員工正在依法怠工，也就是只做嚴格屬於自己職責的工作。
住房部說，負責收集數據的九個區域議會並未全部交回數字。
這些議會統計住在由國家出資的緊急安置住所裡的人數。
住房部長詹姆斯．布朗週日在RTÉ電台談到這次延誤。
他說數據無法公布令他感到沮喪。
他解釋，人們可能進進出出無家可歸的狀態，所以住房部必須仔細確認沒有人被重複計算或遺漏。
他無法說出數字何時能準備好，但承諾會盡快公布。
上一次的官方數據（八月）顯示，有創紀錄的17,885人住在緊急安置住所。
其中12,055人是成人，5,830人是兒童。
布朗也表示，緊急安置住所中非愛爾蘭公民的比例大幅上升。
全國這類住所中約有一半的人不是愛爾蘭公民，在都柏林這個比例是58%。
他說這些人完全有權獲得住房，但他們往往更難負擔一個家。
部長說，可出租的房屋太少，尤其是在都柏林，這使得家庭很難搬離緊急安置住所。
社會民主黨先前要求他清楚說明九月的數據何時公布。

paragraphs: The Department of Housing has failed to publish its monthly homelessness figures on schedule, blaming ongoing industrial action in the public sector.

The figures, which were due on Friday, rely on returns from nine regional lead authorities that report how many people are living in State-funded emergency accommodation. The department said it had not received data from all of them because staff are operating a work-to-rule.

Speaking on RTÉ Radio 1's This Week, Minister for Housing James Browne said he was frustrated by the delay. Because people move in and out of homelessness, he said, officials must avoid double counting and make sure that everyone is included. He was unable to give a release date, saying only that the figures would be published as soon as possible, and admitted he did not know whether they would show a rise or a fall.
The most recent official data, covering August, recorded 17,885 people in emergency accommodation, a record high. The total included 12,055 adults and 5,830 children.

Mr Browne also revealed that the proportion of non-Irish citizens in emergency accommodation has increased significantly. Nationally, they make up around half of those in such accommodation, rising to 58 per cent in Dublin. He stressed that they have every right to housing, but said they tend to face greater financial challenges in securing a home.

He pointed to a severe shortage of private rental properties, particularly in the capital, which makes it harder to move families out of emergency accommodation through the Housing Assistance Payment scheme. The Social Democrats had urged him to clarify when the September figures would appear.
sentZh: 住房部未能如期公布每月無家可歸人數，並將原因歸咎於公部門持續的勞資爭議行動。
這些原定週五公布的數據，仰賴九個區域主導機關提交的報表，內容是住在國家出資緊急安置住所的人數。
住房部表示，由於員工正在依法怠工，尚未收到所有機關的數據。
住房部長詹姆斯．布朗在RTÉ第一電台的《本週》節目中表示，他對延誤感到沮喪。
他說，因為人們會進出無家可歸的狀態，官員必須避免重複計算，並確保每個人都被納入。
他無法給出公布日期，只說會盡快發布，並坦承不知道數字會上升還是下降。
最新的官方數據涵蓋八月，記錄到17,885人住在緊急安置住所，創歷史新高。
總數包括12,055名成人和5,830名兒童。
布朗也透露，緊急安置住所中非愛爾蘭公民的比例已顯著增加。
在全國，他們約佔這類住所人數的一半，在都柏林則升至58%。
他強調他們完全有權獲得住房，但表示他們在取得住所時往往面臨較大的經濟困難。
他指出私人出租房屋嚴重短缺，尤其是在首都，使得透過住房補助計畫讓家庭搬離緊急安置住所更加困難。
社會民主黨曾敦促他說明九月數據何時公布。

paragraphs: Ireland's monthly homelessness figures have been held up indefinitely, with the Department of Housing attributing the delay to industrial action that is gripping parts of the public service.

The statistics, which had been scheduled for release on Friday, are compiled from returns submitted by nine regional lead authorities, each of which tallies the number of people housed in State-funded emergency accommodation. With staff adhering to a work-to-rule, the department has yet to receive a complete set of returns.

Interviewed on RTÉ Radio 1's This Week, the Minister for Housing, James Browne, voiced his frustration at the hold-up. Given that people drift in and out of homelessness, he argued, officials must guard against double counting and ensure that no one slips through the net. He declined to commit to a publication date, pledging merely to release the figures at the earliest opportunity, and conceded he had no idea whether they would point upwards or downwards.
The latest published data, for August, put the number in emergency accommodation at an unprecedented 17,885, comprising 12,055 adults and 5,830 children.

The minister also disclosed that non-Irish citizens now account for a markedly larger share of those in emergency accommodation: roughly half nationwide and 58 per cent in Dublin. While insisting that they are fully entitled to housing, he noted that they are frequently hampered by steeper socio-economic obstacles when trying to secure a home.

He singled out an acute dearth of private rental properties, especially in the capital, as a key impediment to moving families on through the Housing Assistance Payment scheme. The Social Democrats had pressed him to clarify when the September figures would surface.
sentZh: 愛爾蘭每月的無家可歸人數已被無限期延後，住房部將延誤歸因於正困擾部分公共服務的勞資爭議行動。
這些原定週五發布的統計數據，是根據九個區域主導機關提交的報表彙編而成，各機關負責清點住在國家出資緊急安置住所的人數。
由於員工堅持依法怠工，住房部至今尚未收齊所有報表。
住房部長詹姆斯．布朗在RTÉ第一電台《本週》節目受訪時，表達了對延誤的不滿。
他認為，既然人們會不定地進出無家可歸狀態，官員必須防範重複計算，並確保沒有人被遺漏。
他拒絕承諾公布日期，只保證會盡早發布，並承認自己完全不知道數字會往上還是往下。
最新公布的八月數據顯示，緊急安置住所的人數達到空前的17,885人，包括12,055名成人和5,830名兒童。
部長也透露，非愛爾蘭公民目前在緊急安置住所中所佔的比例明顯更高：全國約一半，都柏林則為58%。
他堅稱這些人完全有權獲得住房，但也指出，他們在設法取得住所時常受到更嚴峻的社會經濟障礙所阻。
他特別點出私人出租房屋極度短缺（尤其是在首都），是透過住房補助計畫讓家庭遷出的主要障礙。
社會民主黨曾向他施壓，要求說明九月數據何時出爐。

paragraphs: The publication of Ireland's monthly homelessness statistics has been postponed, with the Department of Housing attributing the delay to industrial action currently affecting the public sector.

These statistics are contingent upon returns from nine regional lead authorities, which collectively record the number of individuals residing in State-funded emergency accommodation. As staff are adhering to a work-to-rule, the department has consequently been unable to obtain a comprehensive data set.

In an interview on RTÉ Radio 1's This Week, the Minister for Housing, James Browne, acknowledged his frustration. He emphasised that, since individuals frequently move in and out of homelessness, rigorous verification is essential to prevent duplication and to ensure that every person is accounted for. Nevertheless, he was unable to specify a publication date and conceded that he could not predict whether the figures would increase or decrease.
The most recent official data, relating to August, indicated that a record 17,885 people were in emergency accommodation, of whom 12,055 were adults and 5,830 were children.

Furthermore, the minister reported a substantial increase in the proportion of non-Irish citizens in emergency accommodation, which now stands at approximately 50 per cent nationally and 58 per cent in Dublin. He maintained that these individuals are fully entitled to housing; however, he noted that they typically encounter more significant socio-economic barriers to obtaining a home.

He identified the severe scarcity of private rental properties, particularly in the capital, as a principal obstacle to relocating families via the Housing Assistance Payment scheme. The Social Democrats had previously called on him to clarify the release date for the September figures.

這些統計數據取決於九個區域主導機關的報表，這些機關共同記錄住在國家出資緊急安置住所的人數。
由於員工堅持依法怠工，住房部因此無法取得完整的數據。
住房部長詹姆斯．布朗在RTÉ第一電台《本週》節目的訪談中，坦承自己感到沮喪。
他強調，由於人們經常進出無家可歸的狀態，嚴格的核實對於防止重複計算、確保每個人都被計入至關重要。
儘管如此，他無法明確給出公布日期，並承認無法預測數字會增加還是減少。
最新的官方數據（八月）顯示，有創紀錄的17,885人住在緊急安置住所，其中12,055人是成人，5,830人是兒童。
此外，部長指出緊急安置住所中非愛爾蘭公民的比例大幅增加，目前全國約為50%，都柏林則為58%。
他堅持這些人完全有權獲得住房；然而他也指出，他們在取得住所時通常會遇到更大的社會經濟障礙。
他認為私人出租房屋嚴重稀缺（尤其在首都），是透過住房補助計畫安置家庭的主要障礙。
社會民主黨先前曾呼籲他說明九月數據的公布日期。
